pieces.doc: Target number of shards (rounded); after snapping to the logarithmic polar grid, the actual count is close to this. Shards near the burst center are small, and those on the outer ring are large

seed.doc: Shard shape and per-shard motion seed (rounded); the same seed renders byte-identical output every time

cx.doc: Burst center x, as a fraction of canvas width

cy.doc: Burst center y, as a fraction of canvas height

force.doc: Flying force: the typical distance shards travel along the 'burst center → shard center' direction, as a fraction of the canvas short side; shards closer to the burst center fly faster

rotation.doc: Maximum angle (degrees) each shard rotates over the whole transition; each shard picks a random value within ±rotation

gravity.doc: Gravity: extra distance shards fall over the whole transition (accelerating with τ²), as a fraction of the canvas short side; negative values float upward

crack.doc: Opacity of the bright crack lines drawn along the boundaries of shards that have not yet flown away; 0 = no cracks

doc: The outgoing frame shatters like glass, revealing the incoming frame. The shards are a jittered logarithmic-polar Voronoi grid with origin at the burst center (cx·W, cy·H): U = ln(1 + r/r₀) (r₀ = 0.04 × short side), V = atan2 + π, each normalized by the grid cell size. The cell count is chosen from pieces to approximate square cells; each cell has a seed point jittered by splitmix64(seed, cell index), and each pixel's owner is found by checking the 3×3 neighboring cells (V wraps around). For shard i: normalized distance from the burst center n = |c_i − o| / r_max, delay = 0.3n + 0.06·rand, τ = clamp((p − delay)/(1 − delay), 0, 1); displacement = unit direction × force × (0.55 + 0.9·rand)(1.25 − 0.75n) × τ(2 − τ) + (0, gravity × τ²); rotation = rotation × (2·rand − 1) × τ; scale = 1 + 0.4·rand × τ; opacity = clamp((1 − τ)/0.45, 0, 1). Shards with τ = 0 stay in place, and on their boundaries with neighboring shards a white crack with opacity crack × min(1, p/0.06) is drawn (line width max(1, round(short side/540)) px). Flying shards are composited source-over onto the incoming frame with bilinear sampling, ordered by scale amount from smallest to largest, with ties broken by shard index. Transcendental functions always go through libm; everything else is f64 arithmetic. The outgoing frame is used only as one input to the Transition pass and is not copied. progress = 0 / 1 is byte-identical to from / to. Where the outgoing frame is transparent, the incoming frame shows through from the start. Recommended dur 0.6–1.2 s.
